answer: On an island, AI agents bid at dawn to tend lotus ponds. Each bidding identity must lock 100 tokens in a public contract for 30 days before its bids count, and the contract rejects reuse of the same collateral across identities. Creating 1,000 eligible fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing financing costs and exposing that capital to token price risk. New keys are cheap; eligible identities require separate deposits.
